rules.title: Document unreasonable noise and report it live
rules.summary: San Jose prohibits disturbing or unreasonably loud noise that disrupts a neighborhood. Music or instruments violate the rule when disturbing or unreasonably loud to a reasonable person outside the facility or unit where the sound originates; the same outside-listener test applies to shouting, screaming, wailing, and other vocalization. These examples are not exclusive. A loudspeaker or amplifier projecting sound outside a building or outdoors requires a police permit. The code has no fixed citywide dB threshold for ordinary neighborhood noise.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact start and stop times, repetition, where you heard it outside the source facility or unit, and how it disturbed the neighborhood. Note the number of people, dangerous conditions, other possible crimes, and any apparent loudspeaker permit.
rules.nextAction: While the disturbance is happening, call San Jose Police at 408-277-8900 and provide the location and incident details. You may remain anonymous, but the Police Department warns that an officer ordinarily will not respond when the caller is anonymous or unavailable for contact. Call 911 only for imminent danger to life or property.

rules.title: Check the 30/60-minute barking test
rules.summary: Antioch's current code prohibits allowing a dog's barking, baying, crying, howling, or other noise to disturb a person at any hour for at least 30 continuous minutes, or for at least 60 intermittent minutes during a 24-hour period. It sets no dB threshold. Noise caused by trespassing, threatened trespassing, teasing, or provocation is excluded. The published Animal Services procedure says an initial complaint produces a notice letter and a 15-day follow-up. If the problem continues or increases, an Animal Control Officer conducts a 30-minute sit-and-listen; the procedure calls for an administrative citation when the officer personally observes 30 continuous minutes. If the officer does not observe that, Animal Services may direct the resident to civil court.
rules.captureInstruction: Log the source address and every date, start time, stop time, and duration so the record shows either 30 continuous minutes or 60 intermittent minutes within 24 hours. Describe how the noise disturbed you and any apparent trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. A complaint must include your name, address, phone number, the address where the dog is kept, and a description of the barking.
rules.nextAction: File the complaint by phone or in person with Antioch Animal Services at 925-779-6989. Keep the barking log after the first complaint. The department accepts another new complaint after 30 calendar days and may use a second sit-and-listen.

rules.title: Document unreasonable noise; no fixed dB cutoff

It prohibits unreasonably loud, disturbing, or unnecessary noise that disturbs the peace, quiet, or comfort of the community or a neighborhood. Listed examples include playing a radio, stereo, phonograph, orchestra, or other musical device in a loud or disturbing manner and continuing a necessary noise longer than necessary. A loudspeaker or amplifier may not project sound outside a building or vehicle except for a public event or dissemination of matters of general public interest, and then only with a permit from the Chief of Police.

Note whether a loudspeaker or amplifier projected sound outdoors and whether a qualifying public event and police permit were present. A phone dB estimate may support the report, but Antioch's rule supplies no number for the phone to decide.

rules.title: Check persistence, property-line disturbance, and the warning
rules.summary: Oakland prohibits keeping an animal or bird that howls, barks, meows, squawks, or makes other annoying noises continuously or incessantly for an unreasonable period so as to create a noise disturbance across a real-property line. The animal rule has no fixed minute or dB threshold. Noise caused by trespass, threatened trespass, teasing, or provocation is excluded. After an official determines that a Chapter 8.18 violation exists, an investigating official must issue a written or verbal warning; a violation occurs if the disturbance persists for more than 15 minutes after that warning or recurs within one week.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, every exact start and stop time, duration, repeated pattern, and whether the noise was audible across the property line. Note any trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. Preserve recordings from the affected property. If an official issues a warning, record who issued it and when, then document any persistence beyond 15 minutes or recurrence within one week. A phone dB estimate does not determine this no-fixed-dB animal rule.
rules.nextAction: Call Oakland Animal Control at 510-535-4884; the City's current Animal Ordinance page directs barking and noisy-animal reports to that number. Give the address, dates, durations, property-line impact, and any prior warning. For an aggressive, abused, sick, injured, or neglected animal, the City instead directs residents to Police Dispatch at 510-777-3333.

rules.title: Check character, duration, warning, receiving zone, and ambient sound
rules.summary: Oakland defines annoying noise as repetitive, shrill, or static-like sound, including loud music. Excessive noise is unnecessary noise persisting for at least 10 minutes; an officer need not witness that period when occupants of two or more separate housing or commercial units certify it with particular details. Mechanical or electronic amplification into public streets that produces excessive or annoying noise is prohibited. Separately, persistent raucous or nerve-racking human, animal, or mechanical noise from 9:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. is a nuisance when it disturbs peace or comfort or injures health. After an official determines a Chapter 8.18 violation exists, an official warning is required; a violation occurs if the disturbance persists more than 15 minutes afterward or recurs within one week. Planning Code receiving-property limits also depend on zone, cumulative minutes per hour, day or night, ambient sound, and sound character. Residential/civic levels range from 60/45 dBA for the 20-minute row to 80/65 dBA for the zero-minute row, daytime/nighttime; day is 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. Commercial levels range 65–85 dBA and industrial levels 70–90 dBA. A higher measured ambient level replaces the listed level, and simple tones, speech or music, and recurring impulse noise reduce each listed standard by 5 dBA.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and receiving addresses, receiving-property zone, exact start and stop times, cumulative duration within one hour, sound character, and how it affected peace, comfort, or health. Ask a second affected household or business to keep its own particular log when applicable. Record any official warning and any persistence beyond 15 minutes or recurrence within one week. The code measurement is A-weighted at the receiving property, generally slow response (fast for impulses), with the microphone four to five feet high and, where possible, at least 10 feet from a reflective surface; ambient sound must also be established. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not the complete prescribed test.
rules.nextAction: For an active disturbance, call Oakland Police non-emergency at 510-777-3333, available 24 hours. For ongoing private-property music or equipment noise, file a Code Enforcement property complaint through Oakland's Accela portal. Include the address, duration, affected receiving zone, second-unit evidence if available, and any warning already issued.

rules.title: Check activity, project duration, receiving zone, permit, and measurement
rules.summary: Oakland has no blanket hours ban for ordinary building construction; sound limits and any project Conditions of Approval control. For construction lasting less than 10 days, Planning Code daytime limits are 80 dBA at residential receiving property and 85 dBA at commercial or industrial receiving property on weekdays 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.; weekend/federal-holiday 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. limits are 65 and 70 dBA. For construction lasting 10 days or more, the corresponding limits are 65/70 dBA on weekdays and 55/60 dBA on weekends. Outside those windows, construction must meet the applicable nighttime receiving-zone table. A higher measured ambient level replaces the listed limit, and simple tones, speech or music, and recurring impulses reduce it by 5 dBA. Grading has separate hours: weekdays 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m., Saturday 8:30 a.m.–6:00 p.m., and none on Sundays or holidays. The City's enforcement page also publishes a residential guideline of 70 dB for no more than five minutes in one hour from 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. Conditions of Approval may be stricter. Engines must be muffled and maintained, unnecessary idling is prohibited, stationary equipment must be placed as far from residences as practical, quiet equipment must be selected where possible, and pile drivers and jackhammers are prohibited Sundays and holidays except emergencies or advance Building Official approval.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit number, posted Conditions of Approval, whether the activity is grading or building, whether the operation lasts under 10 days or at least 10 days, receiving-property zone, exact day and times, equipment, and cumulative duration within one hour. The code measurement is A-weighted at the receiving property, generally slow response (fast for impulses), with the microphone four to five feet high and, where possible, at least 10 feet from reflective surfaces; record ambient sound separately. Also document muffling, idling, equipment placement, and any Sunday/holiday approval. A phone estimate cannot determine this multi-part rule by itself.
rules.nextAction: File the construction-noise complaint through Oakland's exact Accela Code Enforcement form. The City's current complaint line is 510-238-3381. Include the permit or project address, activity type, operation duration, receiving zone, exact times, measurements and ambient method, equipment behavior, and any Conditions of Approval.

rules.title: Check zone, duration, ambient sound, and conduct
rules.summary: San Mateo measures noise on affected property. Base limits are: single-family Zone 1, 60 dB day/50 night; mixed or multifamily Zone 2, 60/55; commercial Zone 3, 65/60; industrial Zone 4, 70 at any time. Day is 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. A source may exceed the applicable base by 5 dB for up to 15 cumulative minutes per hour, 10 dB for up to five minutes, 15 dB for up to one minute, but may never exceed base or measured ambient plus 20 dB. A higher six-minute ambient level replaces the base. Independently of dB, willful loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise disturbing a reasonable person in an adjacent home or business is a nuisance at any hour; additional nighttime music and gathering rules apply 11:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Amplified-sound equipment is generally limited to 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 10:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Sundays and legal holidays.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, affected property's noise zone, exact times, and cumulative duration within one hour. The code measurement uses a Type 1 precision meter, A-weighted slow maximum, five feet above ground. Ambient is a separate six-minute average at the same location with the source silent. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement. Also document how the noise disturbed an adjacent residence or business and any special-event or exception permit.
rules.nextAction: For an active nuisance noise complaint, call San Mateo Police non-emergency. The City's Who to Call page lists police@cityofsanmateo.org next to the non-emergency line for written, non-urgent reports.

hoursRule.context: Municipal Code Chapter 7.30: loud and unreasonable noise, and parties with a band or amplification, in these hours are violations regardless of the dB reading when they disturb persons of ordinary sensitivity; continuing after a peace officer's notice is prima facie willful.
hoursRule.sourceQuote: … to maliciously and willfully generate loud and unreasonable noise, between the hours of eleven p.m. and seven a.m. Noise is "loud and unreasonable" for the purposes of this section, if it disturbs the peace, quiet, or repose of persons of ordinary and normal sensitivity in the neighborhood, regardless of the dB reading.

ambientRecipe.note: San Mateo Municipal Code 7.30 measures ambient as the average over six minutes with a precision meter, slow response, A-weighted, source silent, same spot. The standard is the table level, or the ambient when it is higher, plus 5, 10, 15 or 20 dB depending on how many minutes per hour the noise lasts.
ambientRecipe.sourceQuote: "Ambient" means the average sound level during a six-minute period as measured with a precision sound level meter, using slow response and "A" weighting. The sound level shall be determined with the noise source at issue silent and in the same location as the measurement of the noise level of the source or sources at issue.

meterLimit.comparisonContext: San Mateo Table 7.30.040 Noise Zone 1 base (single-family), measured on the affected property; the base may be exceeded by 5 dB for 15 cumulative minutes an hour, 10 dB for 5 minutes, 15 dB for 1 minute, and never by 20 dB; a higher six-minute ambient replaces it. Phone estimate at your spot, not the officer's meter at the code's measurement point.

rules.title: Check the permit, schedule, equipment, and position
rules.summary: Construction, alteration, repair, or land development authorized by a valid San Mateo permit is generally allowed weekdays 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., Saturdays 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., and Sundays and holidays noon–4:00 p.m.; the permit may authorize or restrict different hours. During allowed work, the ordinance requires at least one of two 90 dB conditions: no individual equipment above 90 dB at 25 feet, or no project noise above 90 dB outside the project property plane. Pile drivers, steam shovels, pneumatic hammers, derricks, hoists, and similar loud equipment are separately prohibited 7:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Utilities, street repairs, street sweepers, garbage service, emergencies, and approved exception permits have separate treatment.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit number and posted hours, equipment, exact start and stop times, day or holiday, and whether an exception applies. The code requires a Type 1 precision meter using A-weighted slow maximum, five feet above ground. If safe, document whether a reading was about 25 feet from one machine or outside the project property plane. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement.
rules.nextAction: For active construction or landscape noise, San Mateo directs nuisance calls to Police non-emergency at 650-522-7700. Give the site, permit information, exact time, equipment, measurement position, and any apparent exception. The City's Who to Call page lists police@cityofsanmateo.org next to the non-emergency line for written, non-urgent reports.

hoursRule.context: Municipal Code Chapter 7.30 for construction under a city permit, and only while equipment stays under 90 dB at 25 feet or 90 dB at the property plane; the permit can set other hours. Holidays use the Sunday hours.
hoursRule.sourceQuote: Construction, alteration, repair or land development activities which are authorized by a valid city permit shall be allowed on weekdays between the hours of seven a.m. and seven p.m., on Saturdays between the hours of nine a.m. and five p.m., and on Sundays and holidays between the hours of noon and four p.m., or at such other hours as may be authorized or restricted by the permit, if they meet at least one of the following noise limitations: (1) No individual piece of equipment shall produce a noise level exceeding 90 dB at a distance of 25 feet.

rules.title: Document habitual, unnecessary, and unreasonable animal noise
rules.summary: Hayward's Animal Control Ordinance makes it unlawful to keep an animal or combination of animals that habitually, unnecessarily, and unreasonably disturbs the peace and quiet of any neighborhood or person by howling, barking, crying, baying, crowing, or other noise. Preserve recordings from the affected location and note any apparent outside influence on the animal. rules.title: Check source property, measurement, reasonable-person factors, and warning
rules.summary: Hayward's dB limits depend on the property producing the noise and the prescribed measurement position. Noise produced on residential property may not exceed 70 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. or 60 dBA from 9:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. at any point outside that source property's plane. On multifamily property, it may not exceed 60 dBA inside another unit on the same property, measured three feet from walls, floor, or ceiling with doors and windows closed. Commercial or industrial source property is limited to 70 dBA outside its property plane, but property abutting residential property uses the residential limits. Public-property noise is generally limited to 60 dBA at 25 feet or more; City activities are exempt. Separately, willfully or negligently producing unreasonable noise at any time violates the ordinance without a meter, based on one or more of 17 factors including audible distance, pitch, unusual nature, rhythm, recurrence, necessity, proximity, affected people, zone, background, time, day, and duration. For a measured dB violation, an officer may warn or cite. For the no-meter test, an officer who perceives a violation may issue a written warning; if a second complaint arrives within 72 hours, signed statements from at least two complainants at different addresses can support a citation.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source and affected addresses, source property type, whether commercial or industrial property abuts residential property, exact times, duration, audible distance, pitch, rhythm, recurrence, background, affected people, and effect on quiet enjoyment. For the dB route, the code requires a Type 1 or Type 2 A-weighted meter, slow response except fast for impulse or rapidly varying noise. Outside, the microphone must be at least four feet high, at least 4.5 feet from walls or similar reflectors, and protected from wind and extraneous sound. Inside, average at least three positions, each at least three feet from a wall. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement. Record any written warning and, if noise recurs within 72 hours, obtain separate detailed logs from complainants at different addresses.

For an ongoing private-property or city-code noise issue, use the exact Access Hayward topic below or call Code Enforcement at 510-583-4143. rules.title: Check the permit, schedule, equipment limit, and property-plane limit
rules.summary: Unless a duly issued permit or land-use Condition of Approval provides otherwise, Hayward construction, structural alteration or repair, and landscaping between 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Sundays and holidays must satisfy both limits: no individual device or equipment may exceed 83 dBA at 25 feet, and project noise may not exceed 86 dBA anywhere outside the project's property plane. For equipment housed in a structure, the first measurement is outside the structure as close as possible to 25 feet from the equipment. At all other times, the source-property limits in §4-1.03.1 control; work outside the listed window is therefore not an automatic violation. Those limits vary by residential, multifamily, commercial, industrial, public, and residential-abutting property. Alarms and warning devices, emergency response, lawful unamplified events, public-safety audio, and medically required or outage generators have categorical exemptions. A conditional noise permit may temporarily alter requirements for up to six months when immediate compliance remains impractical or unreasonable after available abatement techniques.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, permit number, posted hours and Conditions of Approval, exact day and start/stop times, whether it is construction, alteration, repair, or landscaping, each device, and the project property plane. If safe, distinguish a reading about 25 feet from one device from a reading outside the property plane. The code requires a Type 1 or Type 2 A-weighted meter, slow response except fast for impulse or rapidly varying noise; exterior microphones must be at least four feet high, 4.5 feet from large reflectors, and protected from wind and extraneous sound. A phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that prescribed measurement. Document any exemption or conditional noise permit.

rules.title: Apply the unreasonable-period rule and complete the two-week journal
rules.summary: Vallejo prohibits allowing an animal or bird to howl, bark, meow, squawk, or make other annoying noise continuously or incessantly for an unreasonable period so as to create a noise disturbance across a residential real-property line. Enforcement may proceed without a warning. If an officer instead gives a written or verbal warning, persistence for more than five minutes afterward or recurrence within one week may lead to a citation. Describe the disturbance to a reasonable person and note any trespass, threat, teasing, or provocation. Preserve recordings from the affected property. The City considers level, usual or unusual character, natural or unnatural origin, background, proximity to sleeping facilities, zone, density, time, duration, recurrence, and commercial or noncommercial source. Amplifying sound into public streets so as to cause a noise disturbance is separately prohibited. Enforcement may proceed without a warning. If an officer uses an intermediate written or verbal warning, persistence for more than five minutes afterward or recurrence within one week may lead to a citation. For regularly occurring noise averaged over an hour, the Zoning Code also applies zone-based limits. Levels that may not be exceeded for more than 30 minutes per hour are: single-unit residential 60 dBA; multiple-unit residential 65; commercial, mixed-use, medical, and office 70 at the source boundary and 60 at a residential-zone boundary; light and general industrial 75 at the source or district boundary and 65 at a residential-zone boundary; and public, community, open-space, and recreation uses 65 at their boundary and 60 at a residential-zone boundary. From 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., nonresidential sources at a residential-zone boundary are limited to 50 dBA or ambient for the five-minute row; residential-zone source limits are reduced by 10 dBA. Incidental, infrequent, or unexpected noise remains governed by Chapter 7.84, and the more restrictive applicable rule controls.

rules.summary: Richmond prohibits loud, raucous, unnecessary, and unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or annoys a reasonable person, and specifically prohibits operating radios, stereos, drums, musical instruments, or similar devices so as to create a noise disturbance. Excessive noise means unnecessary noise lasting at least 10 minutes; an officer need not witness that period if occupants of two or more separate housing or commercial units certify it with particular details. The City also considers volume, background, proximity, zone, density, time, duration, recurrence, commercial character, audibility more than 25 feet beyond an adjoining residential property boundary, intrusiveness, mobility, and people affected. After an official determines that a fixed-location violation exists, an official warning is required; a violation occurs if the disturbance persists for more than five minutes afterward or recurs within 90 days. An enforcing officer may instead choose the §9.52.100 dBA test as the sole test for that incident. Its 30-minute-per-hour source-boundary levels are 55 dBA single-family residential, 55 multifamily, 70 commercial and light-industrial/office-flex, 75 heavy/marine industrial, and 65 public/community/open/recreation. At residential-zone boundaries, commercial and light-industrial/office-flex sources use 60, heavy/marine industrial 65, and public/community/open/recreation 60. From 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., those nonresidential sources at a residential boundary use 50 dBA or ambient for the five-minute row; residential-zone source limits fall 10 dBA. Pure tones, impulses, music, or speech reduce the levels by 5 dBA. rules.title: Check the reasonable-person rule and Animal Services warning-letter process
rules.summary: Santa Rosa City Code § 17-16.110 prohibits keeping or permitting an otherwise lawful animal or fowl whose sound, cry, or behavior causes annoyance or discomfort to a reasonable person of normal sensitiveness in a residential neighborhood. It sets no fixed minute or dB threshold and does not make a preliminary warning part of the violation. Sonoma County Animal Services enforces animal-noise rules for Santa Rosa. Its current process requires the animal's exact street address plus the complainant's name and address; Animal Services then sends the owner a letter stating that allowing an animal to disturb the peace is illegal, offering guidance, and identifying possible consequences. That letter is the agency's initial complaint procedure, not the legal definition of qualifying animal noise. Animal Services says it will not give the complainant's name or contact information to the animal owner, while also warning that public-records law prevents a guarantee that the information will never be disclosed in records.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the animal's exact address, each date, start and stop time, frequency and duration, the sound or behavior, and how it annoyed or caused discomfort to a reasonable person in the residential neighborhood. Preserve audio, video, your Animal Services case information, and any known warning-letter history.
rules.nextAction: Call Sonoma County Animal Services with the animal's exact address and your name and address to start the warning-letter process. Use the official issue page to review the current process and service hours. Sonoma County Animal Services also takes the report by email at theanimalshelter@sonomacounty.gov; include the animal's exact address and your name and address.

rules.title: Check reasonable-person disturbance, zone, time, property line, and amplified-sound rules
rules.summary: Santa Rosa prohibits willfully making or continuing loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or causes discomfort or annoyance to a reasonable person of normal sensitiveness. The City considers level, intensity, usual or unusual character, natural or unnatural origin, background, sleeping facilities, zoning, population density, time, duration, recurrence, and commercial character. In a residential zone, a radio, musical instrument, television, or similar device may not disturb neighboring residents; exceeding the code's ambient-base level by more than 5 dB at the property line, or inside an adjoining apartment or condominium, is prima facie evidence. For R1/R2 areas, that means more than 50 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., 55 dBA from 7:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m., or 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. For multifamily areas, it means more than 55 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. or 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. A reading at or below those numbers does not prove compliance because the separate reasonable-person test still applies. Sound measurements must use A weighting and slow response on a meter meeting the City's stated standard at the legally relevant property line or adjoining unit. Separate amplified-sound rules generally limit operation to 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; commercial amplified sound is prohibited Sundays and legal holidays, noncommercial amplified sound is allowed 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on those days, and the City Manager may waive the hours. Amplified sound may not exceed the applicable ambient base by 15 dB, operate within 200 feet of a church, school, or hospital, or be unreasonably loud or disturbing. Amplification directed to people on a street, alley, sidewalk, park, or other public property requires Police registration three days beforehand. Chapter 17-16 does not require a preliminary warning before a violation; after notification to desist, each day the violation continues is a separate offense.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and zone, affected property line or adjoining unit, exact time and duration, recurrence, how it disturbed a reasonable person, and whether sound amplification, a public location, registration, waiver, school, church, or hospital is involved. Preserve audio and video. For supporting measurements, record the A-weighted slow-response meter model, calibration, exact position, and applicable code period.
rules.nextAction: Call Santa Rosa Police Non-Emergency while a party or neighborhood disturbance is active. For a recurring property or equipment violation, submit the City's Code Investigation Request Form; staff generally sends the first inspection notice or owner letter within two weeks.

rules.summary: Santa Rosa's citywide noise chapter does not establish one universal construction-hours schedule or a construction-equipment-specific maximum. Individual permits, conditions of approval, and environmental documents may impose project-specific hours or limits and must be checked. Citywide, § 17-16.120 prohibits machinery or equipment noise at a property line more than 5 dB above the code's ambient-base level. The resulting limits are 50 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., 55 dBA from 7:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m., and 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. in R1/R2 areas; 55 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. and 60 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. in multifamily areas; 60 dBA at night and 65 dBA by day in office/commercial areas; 60 dBA at night and 70 dBA by day in intensive-commercial areas; and 75 dBA at any time in industrial areas. Measurements must use A weighting and slow response on a meter meeting the City's stated standard at the property line. Separately, § 17-16.040 prohibits loud, unnecessary, or unusual noise that disturbs neighborhood peace or annoys a reasonable person, considering level, intensity, character, background, sleeping facilities, zoning, density, time, duration, recurrence, and commercial nature. Therefore, being below the machinery number or working during a project-approved hour does not by itself prove compliance. Chapter 17-16 does not require a preliminary warning before a violation; once notification to desist is given, each day the violation continues is a separate offense. The City's complaint form says the first inspection or owner notification letter is generally sent within two weeks.

rules.title: Check the continuous 10-minute rule and staged warning process
rules.summary: San Francisco defines a barking dog as one that barks, bays, cries, howls, or makes other noise continuously and incessantly for 10 minutes to the disturbance of another person. There is no dB threshold. It is not a violation while someone is trespassing or threatening to trespass, or while someone is teasing or provoking the dog. Under Health Code § 41.12(e), two unrelated people living in different households within 300 feet who are disturbed may sign affidavits and ask a police officer to cite the owner or guardian. The City's current complaint process starts by calling 311: 311 records the complaint, and Animal Care and Control and Police issue warning letters for the first two complaints. If the problem continues, the complainant may go to a local police station with a neighbor to file a report that may trigger a citation. Police ordinarily do not dispatch solely for barking without a public-safety threat or animal-endangerment issue.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the exact dog address, start and stop times proving 10 uninterrupted minutes, every break in barking, what disturbance it caused, whether trespass or provocation was involved, 311 case numbers and warning history, and contact information for a second unrelated household within 300 feet if seeking a citation.
rules.nextAction: Call 311 with the dog's exact address to create the complaint record and begin the City's warning-letter process. After the first two complaints, take a neighbor from a different household within 300 feet to a local police station if the qualifying barking continues.

rules.title: Check disturbance, distance, source property, ambient, permit, and measurement
rules.summary: Police Code § 49 prohibits a radio, television, musical instrument, sound system, or similar device that produces raucous noise, disturbs neighborhood peace and comfort, or is louder than necessary. Between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., plainly audible sound 50 feet from the source property's boundary is prima facie evidence of a violation; exceeding Article 29 at any time is also prima facie evidence. Article 29 limits machine, device, music, or entertainment noise from residential property to 5 dBA above ambient outside its property plane, and on the same multi-unit residential property to 5 dBA above ambient three feet from another unit's wall, floor, or ceiling with its windows and doors closed. Commercial or industrial source property uses 8 dBA above ambient outside its property plane; regulated entertainment also has an 8 dBC low-frequency test. Public-property equipment uses 10 dBA above ambient at 25 feet or more. A fixed source inside a residential sleeping or living room is limited to 45 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. and 55 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m., measured with windows open unless mechanical ventilation lets them remain closed. A City permit with different noise limits controls, and an agency may grant a variance. The legal tests use a Type 1 precision meter: at least 10 minutes of ambient with the source silent and at least one minute for the source, plus prescribed outdoor or indoor microphone positions. Neither § 49 nor Article 29 requires a preliminary warning before a violation. A phone's maximum reading by itself cannot decide these tests.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and property type, exact time, how it disturbed people, whether it was plainly audible 50 feet beyond the source property after 10:00 p.m., and any permit. Preserve audio and video. For supporting measurements, document at least one minute with the source and 10 minutes of ambient with it silent, the property plane or interior position, distance, doors and windows, meter type, and calibration.
rules.nextAction: Call Police Non-Emergency while an unreasonable neighbor or party disturbance is in progress. Use the City's exact noise form for equipment, businesses, permitted entertainment, and other listed noise sources.
rules.officialSourceLabel: San Francisco Police Code § 49 and Article 29

ambientRecipe.note: San Francisco Police Code Article 29 measures ambient as the LAeq over at least ten minutes with a Type 1 meter, source silent, same spot, and never below 35 dBA indoors or 45 dBA elsewhere. The residential limit is 5 dBA above that ambient at the property plane.
ambientRecipe.sourceQuote: "Ambient" means LAeq and LCeq values produced during a minimum ten-minute period as measured with a type 1, precision level sound meter, using "A" and "C" frequency weighting. The minimum sound level shall be determined with the noise source at issue silent, and in the same location as the measurement of the noise level of the source or sources at issue. However, for purposes of this Article 29, in no case shall the ambient be considered or determined to be less than: (1) 35 dBA for interior residential noise, and (2) 45 dBA in all other locations. … No person shall produce or allow to be produced by any machine, or device, music or entertainment or any combination of same, on residential property over which the person has ownership or control, a noise level more than five dBA above the ambient at any point outside of the property plane.

rules.summary: Police Code § 2907 prohibits powered construction equipment above 80 dBA at 100 feet, or the equivalent level at another convenient distance. That limit does not apply to impact tools that have approved intake and exhaust mufflers and, for pavement breakers and jackhammers, approved acoustic shields or shrouds; emergency work is also exempt. Construction helicopters are separately limited to two hours in one day and four hours in one week. Section 2908 prohibits building or structure construction, demolition, excavation, alteration, or repair from 8:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. when it exceeds ambient by 5 dBA at the nearest property plane, unless Public Works or Building Inspection granted a special permit; emergency work is exempt. The City describes 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. work as generally permitted, but daytime timing alone does not satisfy the equipment limit, permit conditions, or a variance. The legal tests use a Type 1 precision meter, at least one minute for source noise, at least 10 minutes of ambient with the source silent, and prescribed microphone placement. rules.title: Check habitual or nuisance barking and the five-person abatement route
rules.summary: Daly City prohibits an owner or caretaker from permitting an animal to habitually bark, meow, disturb a citizen's peace, or become a public nuisance. It separately declares excessive, continuous, or untimely barking to be a nuisance. Neither rule sets a fixed minute or dB threshold. A separate abatement procedure applies when five or more people with separate residences, or five or more people regularly employed in the neighborhood, affirm in writing that the animal is an habitual nuisance; if the poundmaster finds the nuisance exists, the owner or custodian is served notice to abate it. The five-person requirement belongs to that abatement route and is not the definition of every animal-noise violation. An animal-control, humane, or peace officer may issue an administrative citation after determining that the animal-control chapter was violated; the chapter does not require a warning before every citation. Peninsula Humane Society states that it is not contracted to handle barking complaints and that each city handles them itself.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the animal address, every date, start and stop time, breaks, frequency, whether the barking was excessive, continuous, habitual, or untimely, and exactly how it disturbed the peace. For the formal abatement route, preserve signed written statements and addresses or neighborhood workplaces for five separate people.
rules.nextAction: Call the Daly City Police Department non-emergency front desk for the City's barking process and ask where to submit the written statements if using the five-person abatement route. Do not route a barking-only complaint to Peninsula Humane Society.

rules.title: Check public-peace disturbance, nighttime audibility, and amplifier permit
rules.summary: Daly City Municipal Code § 9.22.010 prohibits making, or allowing on premises under one's control, any noise, disorder, or tumult that disturbs the public peace at any time. Section 9.22.030 separately prohibits, from 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m., causing or allowing noise, music, sound, or another disturbance on one's property that may be heard by, disturbs, or harasses another person beyond the property, quarters, or apartment where it originates. No minute or dB threshold appears in these sections. A loudspeaker or sound amplifier projecting sound outside a building or outdoors requires a written Police Chief permit stating the permittee, purpose, authorized time and place, and termination date. Chapter 9.22 does not require a preliminary warning before a violation. A phone reading or the clock alone cannot decide whether the required audibility or disturbance exists or whether a permit applies.

Preserve audio and video from the affected location.

rules.title: Apply the new 2026 hours, daylight-saving schedule, equipment rule, and exemption
rules.summary: Daly City's new Chapter 15.09 applies to outdoor work on private property for a project requiring a building permit. During standard time, work is limited to 8:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. Monday–Friday and 9:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. Saturday and Sunday. During daylight-saving time, the same start times apply but work may continue until 8:30 p.m. Construction is prohibited on federal holidays unless the Building Official or designee grants an exemption. Deliveries of materials or equipment are not allowed outside the applicable hours. Staging and site preparation may begin up to one hour before the start time only if no construction equipment is used; equipment use outside the applicable hours is strictly prohibited. During permitted hours, § 15.09.020 incorporates the temporary construction-noise levels in the General Plan Noise Element. That document identifies earthmoving equipment at 70–95 dBA at 50 feet, impact equipment at 80–105 dBA at 50 feet, and pile driving up to 105 dBA at 50 feet; the chapter does not create one universal phone-meter cutoff for every equipment type and project condition. Required hour signs must be five feet above ground and visible at every construction entrance. A written exemption may be granted for an emergency or exceptional circumstances beyond the applicant's control, must be posted, and may be revoked. Enforcement may include a warning notice, an inspection hold, or a stop-work order; a warning is a possible enforcement action, not a mandatory prerequisite. The general 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m. disturbing-noise rule still applies where relevant.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the address, whether work is outdoors on private property and requires a building permit, date, daylight-saving or standard time, activity and equipment, deliveries or staging, exact start and stop times, distance from the equipment, posted-hours sign, permit conditions, and any posted exemption. Preserve audio, video, and readings from a documented position.
rules.nextAction: Report the construction violation to Code Enforcement through Daly City iHelp, email codeenforcement@dalycity.org, or call 650-991-8260. For a disturbing violation actively occurring during the 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m. police-noise period, call 24-hour dispatch at 650-992-1225.

rules.title: Document frequent or extended barking
rules.summary: Santa Clara prohibits keeping a dog whose loud barking or unusual noises disturb the peace and quiet of one or more people in the immediate neighborhood. Loud barking means barking, howling, or baying by day or night for frequent and/or extended periods that becomes a nuisance and prevents comfortable enjoyment of a home. The rule sets no fixed minute or dB threshold. Barking while the dog is protecting against or resisting a trespasser is excluded; the owner bears the burden of proving that exception.
rules.captureInstruction: Record each date, start and stop time, frequency, duration, source address, and how the noise prevented comfortable enjoyment of your home. Note any apparent trespass or protective response.
rules.nextAction: First try a neighborly request when safe. If habitual barking continues, report it while it is happening to Santa Clara Police/Public Safety Dispatch at 408-615-5580. The Police Department page lists police@santaclaraca.gov under Contact Us; use it for the written log after a live report.

rules.title: Separate fixed-source and conduct rules
rules.summary: Santa Clara's numeric limits apply only to fixed sources and are measured on affected property. Residential receiving zones: 55 dBA from 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. and 50 dBA from 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; commercial/office: 65/60; light industrial: 70 at any time; heavy industrial: 75. Music or informational speech reduces the applicable limit by 5 dBA, while a different ambient level can adjust it in 5 dBA steps. The chapter does not cover mobile sources. Separately, California Penal Code § 415(2) covers malicious and willful loud, unreasonable disturbance. Emergencies, permitted outdoor events, allowed-hours construction, and other listed activities are exempt from the fixed-source chapter.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source, exact time, duration, repetition, affected property's zoning, closest measurement point on affected property, and a background reading. Identify whether the source was fixed or mobile and whether it contained music or speech. Note any emergency, permit, event, or other apparent exemption. A phone estimate is supporting evidence and is not the code-specified sound-level-meter measurement.

rules.title: Document frequent or long-continued animal noise and the officer's notice
rules.summary: San Leandro has two animal-noise rules and neither sets a minute or dB threshold. The Noise Ordinance (§4-1-1115(a), rewritten by Ord. 2024-012) makes it a disturbing, excessive and offensive noise to permit an animal to emit any frequent or long-continued noise that causes annoyance or discomfort to a reasonable person of normal sensitiveness in the vicinity; it does not count if someone is trespassing, threatening to trespass, or teasing or provoking the animal. The animal chapter (§4-11-435(a)) separately makes it a nuisance to knowingly permit an animal, by barking or other noise, to disturb any other person's peace and quiet; a watchdog is allowed only if the keeper quiets it at once and never leaves it unattended where prolonged or repeated barking disturbs anyone. Once an Animal Control Officer tells the owner, orally or in writing, that the animal violated the section, failing to stop the nuisance is itself a violation.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the animal's address, the date, exact start and stop times, how often it recurred, the kind of noise, whether anyone was provoking or trespassing, and how it disturbed your peace and quiet or comfort. A run of dated incidents shows 'frequent or long-continued'. Note whether the owner has already been warned by Animal Control, because a repeat after that notice is its own violation. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule.
rules.nextAction: Call San Leandro Police Animal Control at 510-577-0449 (the City's Report a Concern page lists Animal Control under the Police Department) and ask that the complaint and the owner's notice be documented. For barking happening right now, the City routes noise to Police non-emergency dispatch at 510-577-2740. The MySanLeandro (SeeClickFix) portal has no animal or noise category.

rules.title: Check the 65/55 dB table, the 50-foot night test, and the ambient-plus-5 rule
rules.summary: San Leandro's Noise Ordinance (Article 4-1-11, rewritten by Ord. 2024-012) bans any disturbing, excessive or offensive noise that annoys reasonable persons of normal sensitivity, weighed by eleven factors including level, ambient, time, duration, recurrence and zoning. For music, stereos and electronics (§4-1-1115(e)) it adds three concrete tests. First, playing any radio, TV, audio equipment, drum or instrument between 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. so it is plainly audible 50 feet from the building or vehicle is prima facie evidence of a violation. Second, any such noise that exceeds the ambient level on another occupied property, or inside an adjoining unit of a condo, apartment, duplex or attached business, by more than 5 decibels is a violation. Third, a Table of Applicable Limits sets 65 decibels from 8:01 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and 55 decibels from 10:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. Loudspeakers and band practice between 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. that disturb neighbors are also listed, and motors, engines and mechanical devices are restricted 9:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. unless enclosed so they are not plainly audible at a residential property line. Occasional gatherings and entertainment events between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., permitted special events, and residential property maintenance 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. are exempt. Violations are public nuisances abated under Chapter 1-12.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and property type, exact times, duration, whether it recurred, and how it disturbed you. After 10:00 p.m., step 50 feet from the building or vehicle and note whether the music was plainly audible there. Measure the noise at your spot, then the quiet with the source silent at the same spot, so the difference against the 5 dB ambient rule is visible. The code names no meter type or measurement position, so a phone estimate is supporting evidence; the table limits are the City's numbers, not a promise about your reading.
rules.nextAction: The City's Report a Concern page lists Noise under the Police Department at 510-577-2740; call while the noise is happening so an officer can hear it. The MySanLeandro (SeeClickFix) portal has no noise category, so a written pattern goes in your own log and PDF.

Phone estimate at your spot, not the officer's meter at the code's measurement point.

rules.title: Check the day, the clock, and whether the work is next to homes
rules.summary: San Leandro's Noise Ordinance (§4-1-1115(b), rewritten by Ord. 2024-012) makes construction work or related activity that is adjacent to, or across a street or right-of-way from, a residential use a disturbing, excessive and offensive noise except between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on weekdays and 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on Saturday and Sunday. No such construction is permitted on Federal holidays. 'Construction' covers site preparation, assembly, erection, substantial repair, alteration, demolition or similar action on private property, rights-of-way, streets, structures, utilities or facilities. The rule is hours-only; it sets no dB limit. A violation can be enforced as a public nuisance under Chapter 1-12 and by a stop-work order or revocation of the permits for that project. Separately, motors, engines and mechanical devices are restricted 9:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. (§4-1-1115(c)). Emergency work, public-agency and utility repair operations, and residential property maintenance between 8:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. are exempt, and the City Manager can issue an exception permit for up to six months.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the project address, that it sits next to or across the street from homes, the day of the week, whether it was a Federal holiday, and the exact start and stop times of the work outside the allowed hours. Note the kind of work (demolition, framing, grading) and the permit number from the posted card if visible. A photo or short clip with the time is strong here because the rule turns on the clock, not on dB. A phone dB estimate does not decide this hours-only rule.
rules.nextAction: For work happening outside the allowed hours, call San Leandro Police non-emergency at 510-577-2740; the City's Report a Concern page routes noise to the Police Department. For a project that keeps doing it, the same page lists Building Code Enforcement at BuildingInspections@SanLeandro.org and 510-577-3405, which can issue a stop-work order or pull the permit; send the dated log and PDF.

rules.title: Document prolonged or repeated barking and the owner's response
rules.summary: Livermore Municipal Code §6.04.060(A) makes it unlawful and a nuisance for an owner to knowingly permit an animal, by barking or other noise, to disturb any other person's peace and quiet. The owner must take immediate steps to quiet the animal whenever it creates such a nuisance, and may not leave it unattended where its barking, if prolonged or repeated an undue number of times, disturbs anyone's peace and quiet. The rule sets no minute count or dB threshold. The Police Department's Animal Services page asks you to try the owner first with a note or a word, then file a barking complaint by phone with the dog's exact address and your name and number; Animal Control contacts the owner with education first, and if it keeps up, the reporting person can co-sign a citation and take the matter to court.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the dog's address, the date, exact start and stop times, how long it went on, how many times it happened that day or week, whether anyone was home, and how it disturbed your peace and quiet. Note the date you spoke to or left a note for the owner. Dated repeats show 'prolonged or repeated an undue number of times' and support the citation you may be asked to co-sign. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule.

rules.title: Check disturbance at any hour and the 75-foot test after 11 p.m.
rules.summary: Livermore Municipal Code Chapter 9.36 bans any loud, disturbing, unnecessary, unusual or habitual noise that annoys, disturbs, injures or endangers the comfort, health, repose, peace or safety of other persons in the City (§9.36.020). For radios, musical instruments, phonographs and similar devices (§9.36.090) it is a violation at any time to play them so as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of neighbors, or louder than needed for the people in the room or vehicle who want to hear them. Between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., playing them so they are plainly audible 75 feet from the source or at the property line, whichever is greater, is prima facie evidence of a violation. Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling or singing on public streets is banned 11:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m., or at any time it disturbs people in homes or nearby (§9.36.100). Blowers, fans and combustion engines have their own night and holiday hours (§9.36.040). The chapter has no dB limit; short-term-rental outdoor noise is separately barred 10:00 p.m.–8:00 a.m., and industrial areas more than 500 feet from homes are exempt from the hour limits.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, duration, whether it recurred, and how it disturbed you. After 11:00 p.m., step 75 feet from the source (or to the property line if that is farther) and note whether the music was plainly audible there; that is the code's own test. The code names no meter, position or dB number, so a phone estimate is supporting evidence of how loud it was, not the City's test.
rules.nextAction: While it is happening, call Livermore Police non-emergency dispatch at 925-371-4987 so an officer can hear it. For a pattern, the City's Neighborhood Preservation code violation form has a 'Noise complaints' box for daytime filing; the form itself says to call LPD at 925-371-4987 after 5 p.m. Code Enforcement's phone is 925-960-4444. The form does not process anonymous complaints.

rules.summary: Redwood City adopts the San Mateo County Animal Control Ordinance (County Code Chapter 6.04, as amended January 9, 2024) by reference in City Code §5.1. The City's Animal Control page says the County contracts with the Peninsula Humane Society & SPCA to enforce animal laws, and PHS says it does not take barking complaints and sends them to the local police. Redwood City's noise chapter (Chapter 24) is administered by the Chief of Police.

Note the date you spoke to or left a note for the owner. A pattern across days shows 'habitually'; a single long stretch shows 'continuously'. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule.

rules.title: Check the 8 p.m. clock, three or more people, and 6 dB over the quiet
rules.summary: Redwood City Code Chapter 24 has no fixed dB limit for parties; it works from the local ambient. Between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m., noise from a party, dance, meeting or other gathering of three or more people that is more than 6 dB above the local ambient, measured anywhere in a residential district outside the source property's plane, is an excessive and unreasonable noise (§24.20A). For a gathering on residential property, the same 6 dB test also applies three feet from any wall, floor or ceiling inside another dwelling unit on the same property with doors and windows closed (§24.20B). 'Local ambient' is the lowest level repeating itself over six minutes with a precision meter, source silent, same spot, never below 40 dBA outdoors or 30 dBA indoors (§24.2). Enforcement runs through a written Notice to Abate from the Police: once served, letting the noise continue within the next twelve hours is a violation (§24.21), and the people noticed become liable for the cost of every later police response, arrests and court time, up to $15,000 in collection costs (§24.22). Violations are infractions and public nuisances (§§24.41, 24.42). The chapter is administered by the Chief of Police.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times after 8:00 p.m., how many people were gathered, whether it was inside or outside, and how it disturbed you. Measure the noise at your spot, then run the six-minute quiet baseline at the same spot with the source silent, so the difference against the 6 dB rule is visible. The City's test uses a precision meter at a point outside the property plane; a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement. Note whether police came and whether a written Notice to Abate was given, and log anything after it.
rules.nextAction: While the party is going, call Redwood City Police 24-hour dispatch (non-emergency) at 650-780-7118 so an officer can measure and serve the Notice to Abate; after-hours the Police page also lists 650-780-7100. For a repeat address, file a Noise Complaint (Residential Noise) in myRWC with the dates and the PDF.

rules.title: Check weekday hours, the 110 dB ceiling, and the ten-minute rule
rules.summary: Redwood City Code Chapter 24, Division 3 (amended 2019 and September 2025) limits general construction noise on private projects to weekdays 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; loud or 'excessive or unreasonable' construction noise is limited to weekdays 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; and both are prohibited during holiday periods posted on the City website (§24.32A). Weekends are outside the allowed hours, and the required job-site sign spells it out: noise prohibited Monday–Friday 8:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. and all day Saturdays, Sundays and holidays (§24.33). Preconstruction noise such as deliveries, truck idling, backup beeps, yelling and radios follows the same hours (§24.32B). Any construction noise that persists for ten continuous minutes outside those hours is itself an excessive and unreasonable noise (§24.30B). At all times, construction may not exceed 110 dB measured at any point in a residential district outside the property plane, or 110 dB from a single machine measured 25 feet away (§§24.30, 24.31). 'Construction' includes landscaping and landscaping equipment. Exceptions: emergency work; an owner or resident personally working on their own unit weekdays 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. and weekends and holidays 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. (§24.35); and Building Official approval requested before the work, with a copy kept on site (§24.32C), or an exception permit of up to six months (§24.34). Violations are infractions and public nuisances.

Note the kind of work and equipment, whether a contractor was present (the owner-resident exemption does not cover contractors), and whether the site sign and any approved off-hours letter were posted. The 110 dB ceiling is measured with a precision meter at the property plane or 25 feet from the machine; a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement.

rules.title: Time it: ten minutes straight, or half an hour on and off
rules.summary: Mountain View City Code §5.62 makes it unlawful to keep a dog that disturbs the peace and quiet of one or more persons in the immediate neighborhood by loud barking or unusual noises. 'Loud barking' is defined: barking, howling or baying, by day or night, continuously or incessantly for ten minutes, or intermittently for one-half hour or more, that creates a noise disturbance across a residential or commercial property line. Barking while the dog is protecting its premises against a trespasser does not count, and the owner carries the burden of proving that. The rule sets no dB threshold; the clock is the test. Animal law enforcement in Mountain View is done by the Silicon Valley Animal Control Authority (SVACA), a joint powers authority; the City's Animal Services page lists SVACA at 408-764-0344 and staff@svaca.com, with the Police non-emergency line for urgent after-hours matters.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the dog's address, the date, exact start and stop times, and whether the barking ran ten minutes without a real break or came and went for thirty minutes or more; the app's level trace shows the stretch. Note that nobody was at the fence or gate provoking the dog. A phone dB estimate does not decide this rule; the ten-minute and thirty-minute clocks do.
rules.nextAction: Call SVACA at 408-764-0344 with the dog's exact address and your name and number; SVACA's complaints page says it may ask you to complete its Animal Complaint Form so it can investigate. For a written record, email staff@svaca.com with the dated log and PDF. For an urgent after-hours matter the City points to Mountain View Police at 650-903-6344.

rules.title: State law covers loud parties; the City has no music decibel rule
rules.summary: Mountain View's City Code has no general loud-music or party ordinance: the old noise sections in Chapter 21 (§§21.20, 21.25, 21.27) were repealed in 1997, and what remains regulates stationary equipment (§21.26) and sound trucks (§21.33). Loud parties and music are handled by Mountain View Police under California Penal Code §415(2), which makes it an offense to maliciously and willfully disturb another person by loud and unreasonable noise. That rule applies at any hour and sets no dB cutoff; it turns on conduct and reasonableness. Separately, stationary equipment such as air conditioners, pool pumps and compressors may not exceed 55 dB(A), or 50 dB(A) from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., measured on a receiving residential property with a Type 2 meter (§21.26).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, duration, whether it recurred, what was heard (music, shouting, bass), and how it disturbed you. Note whether the noise continued after a request to stop, because willfulness matters under §415. A phone estimate is supporting evidence of how loud it was; no City number decides a party complaint.
rules.nextAction: While the noise is happening, call Mountain View Police non-emergency at 650-903-6344 so an officer can hear it. For a repeat address, send a Concern to the Police Department through Ask Mountain View with the dates and the PDF.

rules.title: Weekdays 7 to 6 only; equipment limited to 55 by day, 50 at night
rules.summary: Mountain View City Code §8.06.05 (rewritten September 9, 2025) allows construction activity only from 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. No work is permitted on Saturday, Sunday, recognized holidays, or outside those hours without prior written approval from the Chief Building Official, who may also cut or extend hours on 24 hours' notice. 'Construction activity' means any physical activity on the site or staging area, including material deliveries. Emergencies are exempt but must be reported to Police and the Building Division by the next business day. A sign at each vehicle entrance must show the working hours and contacts, and any written order or permit must be produced on request. Recognized holidays include New Year's Day, MLK Day, Presidents Day, Farmworkers Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, and City Hall's closure between Christmas and New Year's. The hours rule sets no dB limit. Separately, stationary mechanical equipment such as air conditioners, pool pumps and compressors may not exceed 55 dB(A), or 50 dB(A) from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m., measured anywhere on a receiving residential property with a Type 2 or better meter (§21.26).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the day, whether it was a holiday, and the exact start and stop times outside 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. weekdays; deliveries count. Note whether the required sign is up and whether the contractor could show a written approval for off-hours work. For a fixed machine (compressor, pump, air conditioner), measure at your property, then measure the quiet with it off; the City measures on the receiving residential property with a Type 2 meter, so a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement.
rules.nextAction: The City's Construction Hours page: during business hours report to the Building Division at 650-903-6313 (Monday–Friday 8–5); after hours, weekends and holidays call Police non-emergency at 650-903-6344, then email the Building Division at cmvworkrequest@mountainview.gov for follow-up. Work in the street or sidewalk goes to Public Works at 650-903-6311.

rules.title: Document frequent barking that disturbs anyone within 300 yards
rules.summary: Milpitas Municipal Code V-210-4.03 (Excessive Noise) says no person owning or controlling an animal may allow it to bark, howl, wail, bay, yelp, cry or make any other noise with such frequency or in such a manner as to disturb the peace and quiet of one or more persons living within 300 yards of the premises where the animal is kept. The rule sets no minute count or dB threshold; frequency and manner are the test, and one disturbed neighbor is enough. Section V-210-4.06 also lets a private person sue under the Civil Code when the nuisance specially injures them. The City's resource directory lists Noise Complaints and Leash Law Enforcement at 408-586-3071; Milpitas contracts animal control field services to San Jose Animal Care & Services.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the animal's address, the date, exact start and stop times, how often it happened that day and that week, and how it disturbed your peace and quiet. Your address within 300 yards of the animal's premises is part of the rule, so note the distance. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule; the dated pattern does.
rules.nextAction: Call Milpitas Code Compliance at 408-586-3071, the number the City lists for noise complaints and leash-law enforcement, with the animal's address and your name and number. For the written pattern, email Code Enforcement at Code_Enforcement@milpitas.gov with the dated log and PDF; the City's Report Violations page names that mailbox for code complaints. The MyMilpitas (SeeClickFix) app has no animal or noise category.

rules.title: Check 65 dB at the line, 3 dB over the quiet, and the 50-foot night test
rules.summary: Milpitas Municipal Code Chapter 213 (Noise Abatement, amended September 2, 2025) works three ways in residential zones. First, any Disturbing Noise that raises the level 3 dB over the ambient, or exceeds 65 dB, measured at the noise source's property line, whichever is stricter, is unlawful (V-213-3.01). Second, a Disturbing Noise is a prima facie violation if it is audible 50 feet from the source property line between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., or 100 feet from the line between 7:01 a.m. and 9:59 p.m.; a moving source uses 100 feet at any hour (V-213-3.03). Third, 'Disturbing Noise' is defined as sound that disturbs a reasonable person of normal sensitivity living in the area, and expressly includes music, TV or speakers played louder than needed for the people in the room, horns, machinery, engine revving, and yelling or singing (V-213-2.04). Ambient is the Leq over at least three minutes with the source silent (V-213-2.01). Outdoor music at restaurants and bars in commercial and mixed-use zones has its own 9:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. window and 65–90 dB limits (V-213-3(b)). A violation is a public nuisance and an infraction, and after a first police warning at a loud or unruly gathering, the second and later police responses are billed to the responsible person (V-213-10, 11).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, duration, what was heard, and how it disturbed you. After 10:00 p.m., step 50 feet from the source property line and note whether the noise was plainly audible there; by day use 100 feet. Measure the noise, then run the three-minute quiet baseline at the same spot with the source silent, so the 3 dB and 65 dB tests are both visible. The City measures at the source's property line; a phone estimate at your spot is supporting evidence, not that measurement.
rules.nextAction: While the noise is happening, call Milpitas Police non-emergency at 408-586-2400 so an officer can hear it and give the first warning. By day, Code Compliance takes noise complaints at 408-586-3071. For a repeat address, email Code Enforcement at Code_Enforcement@milpitas.gov with the dates and the PDF.

It shall also be prima facie violation of this Section if any Disturbing Noise is audible during the hours of 7:01 a.m. to 9:59 p.m. from a distance of 100 feet from the property line of the noise source or any nonstationary noise source.

rules.title: Seven to seven every day, never on the six holidays
rules.summary: Milpitas Municipal Code V-213-3.07 (amended September 2, 2025) allows construction of any building, road, walkway, pool or landscape improvement, and the operations that go with it including delivery of materials, only between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on weekdays and weekends. No construction work may be performed on the Chapter's holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day (V-213-2.07). The rule is hours-only; it sets no dB limit for construction. Exempt (V-213-3.08): emergency work to protect life and property; state-preempted work such as public school construction; utility construction and maintenance; work on an existing single-family or duplex home done by the property owner; right-of-way work the Public Works Director deems necessary; and anything else the City Manager exempts. Construction noise outside the hours is also a Disturbing Noise under the residential-zone rules, and any violation of the Chapter is a public nuisance and an infraction.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the date, whether it was one of the six holidays, and the exact start and stop times before 7:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m.; material deliveries count. Note the kind of work and whether a contractor was present, since the owner-only exemption covers a homeowner working on their own house, not a crew. A time-stamped photo or short clip is strong here because the rule turns on the clock, not on dB. A phone dB estimate does not decide this hours-only rule.
rules.nextAction: Early mornings, evenings and holidays call Milpitas Police non-emergency at 408-586-2400. During business hours Code Compliance takes noise complaints at 408-586-3071. For a project that keeps doing it, email Code Enforcement at Code_Enforcement@milpitas.gov with the dated log and PDF; the City's Report Violations page names that mailbox.

No construction work shall be conducted or performed on the holidays indicated in Section V-213-2-2.05 of this Chapter.

rules.title: Document barking by loudness, duration and location; 60 dBA is the outer bound
rules.summary: Pleasanton Municipal Code §7.08.010 makes it unlawful and a nuisance for an owner to knowingly permit or tolerate an animal, by barking or other noise of such loudness, duration and location, to disturb any reasonable person's peace and quiet. A watchdog is allowed only if the owner quiets it at once whenever it barks and never leaves it unattended where its barking would disturb a reasonable person. That rule has no minute or dB threshold. Separately, the noise chapter's residential limit (§9.04.030) applies to any 'machine, animal, device' on residential property: a noise level over 60 dBA at any point outside the property plane, measured with a Type S2A meter on slow response, is a violation at any hour. Pleasanton's Animal Services Officers are part of the Police Department and enforce the animal code; the City says animal control problems can be reported to Police 24 hours a day.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the dog's address, the date, exact start and stop times, how long it went on, whether anyone was home, and how it disturbed your peace and quiet; loudness, duration and location are the code's own three words. Note the dates you spoke to or left a note for the owner. A phone estimate near the property line is supporting evidence for the 60 dBA animal limit, not the officer's meter reading.
rules.nextAction: Call Pleasanton Police / Animal Services at 925-931-5100, the number the City gives for animal complaints around the clock, with the dog's exact address and your name and number. Keep the dated log for the officer; if the owner is warned and the barking continues, the log carries the case.

rules.title: Check 60 dBA at the property line, any hour
rules.summary: Pleasanton Municipal Code §9.04.030 says no person may produce, on residential property, a noise level over 60 dBA at any point outside the property plane, by any machine, animal, device or combination of them. On multifamily property the same 60 dBA cap applies inside any other dwelling unit, measured at least four feet from walls, floor and ceiling with doors and windows closed. 'Noise level' is the maximum continuous or repetitive peak level on a precision meter, A-weighted, slow response. The limit runs all day and all night; there is no separate night number. One daytime exception: a source that never exceeds 70 dBA at 25 feet is exempt from the residential limit between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. (10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on Sundays and holidays). Commercial property is capped at 70 dBA and industrial at 75 dBA at the property plane, and a business within 300 feet of homes that is open 10:00 p.m.–6:00 a.m. must meet the residential standard at the zoning boundary. Permitted events at the fairgrounds, schools and parks are exempt, and the City Manager may issue an exception permit of up to six months.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address and property type, exact times, duration, and how it disturbed you. Measure as close to the source's property line as you safely can, because the City's number is taken at any point outside the property plane; a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not the Type S2A meter reading. If the noise was before 8:00 p.m., note whether it was still loud 25 feet from the source, which is where the daytime exception is judged.
rules.nextAction: While it is happening, call Pleasanton Police non-emergency at 925-931-5100 so an officer can hear it. For a repeat address, send the dated log and PDF to Code Enforcement through its contact form; the Code Enforcement page lists noise ordinance violations among the issues it handles and gives 925-931-5620 for questions.

rules.title: Check the permit hours and the 83/86 dBA limits; off hours fall to 60
rules.summary: Pleasanton Municipal Code §9.04.100 lets permitted construction, alteration or repair work exceed the normal property limits only between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. daily, and 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on Sundays and holidays, and only if it meets at least one of two limits: no single piece of equipment over 83 dBA at 25 feet (measured outside any structure as near 25 feet as possible), or no more than 86 dBA at any point outside the project's property plane. Outside those hours the ordinary limits apply instead of a ban: 60 dBA at the property plane for residential property (§9.04.030), 70 dBA commercial, 75 dBA industrial. Emergencies and utility standby testing are exempt (§9.04.090), and the City Manager may issue an exception permit of up to six months (§9.04.110). Pool equipment must meet the property's limit and is field-tested before final approval (§9.04.078). The residential limit also reaches machines and devices, so a compressor, pump or air conditioner over 60 dBA at the line is a violation at any hour.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the day, whether it was a Sunday or holiday, the exact start and stop times, and the equipment running. Inside the permit window, a reading near 25 feet from one machine and a reading at the property line map onto the two limits; outside the window, the 60 dBA residential line is the test. The City measures with a Type S2A precision meter on slow response, so a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement. Note the permit number from the posted card if visible.
rules.nextAction: Early mornings, evenings, Sundays and holidays call Pleasanton Police non-emergency at 925-931-5100.
