rules.title: Time it: ten minutes straight, or half an hour on and off
rules.summary: Alameda has two barking rules. The Noise Regulations (§4-10.5(b)(2)) make it a violation to own or harbor an animal that howls, barks, meows or squawks continuously or incessantly for ten minutes, or intermittently for one-half hour or more, creating a noise disturbance across a residential or commercial property line; barking at a trespasser or at someone teasing or provoking the animal does not count. The Animal Control chapter (§7-3.10) separately bans keeping a dog that disturbs the peace and quiet of any neighborhood or person by persistent or prolonged barking, howling or unusual noises, and treats it as a §4-10.5 violation. A 'noise disturbance' is sound that annoys or disturbs a reasonable person of normal sensitivity, weighed by factors such as level over ambient, closeness to bedrooms, number of people affected, time and duration. No dB number decides a barking case; the clocks do. Each day is a separate infraction (§4-10.12). The City's two Animal Control Officers respond to barking complaints and are reached through Alameda Police dispatch.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the dog's address, the date, exact start and stop times, and whether the barking ran ten minutes without a real break or came and went for thirty minutes or more; the app's level trace shows the stretch. Note that nobody was at the fence provoking the dog. Dated repeats show 'persistent or prolonged'. A phone dB estimate does not decide this rule.
rules.nextAction: Call Alameda Police dispatch at 510-337-8340, the number the City's Animal Services page gives for barking complaints and any on-going animal issue, with the dog's exact address and your name and number; an Animal Control Officer is on duty 8:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m. every day. The shelter line is 510-337-8565. Keep the dated log for the officer.

rules.title: Check the minutes-per-hour table; music is held 5 dB lower
rules.summary: Alameda's Noise Regulations (§4-10) set exterior standards measured at the receiving property. For a home, school, hospital, church or library (Table I), the noise may not exceed 55 dB(A) by day (7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.) or 50 dB(A) at night (10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.) for more than 30 cumulative minutes in any hour; 60/55 for 15 minutes; 65/60 for 5 minutes; 70/65 for 1 minute; and 75/70 may never be exceeded. Noise that is mainly music or speech, a pure tone, or recurring impulses is held 5 dB(A) lower. If the ambient is already above a standard, the ambient becomes the standard. Measurements are A-weighted, slow response, anywhere on the affected property, with the microphone 3–5 feet up and 4 feet from reflecting surfaces, after calibration. Separately, playing a radio, TV, drum or instrument so as to create a noise disturbance is a prohibited act at any hour (§4-10.5(b)(1)), and a portable or vehicle radio audible 50 feet away in a public place is a violation (§4-10.5(b)(9)). 'Noise disturbance' means sound that annoys a reasonable person of normal sensitivity, judged by level over ambient, closeness to bedrooms, people affected, time and duration. Recreation programs in City parks 9:00 a.m.–10:15 p.m. are exempt. Each day is a separate infraction and a public nuisance (§4-10.12).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, how many minutes in the hour it ran, and how it disturbed you; the level trace shows the minutes above each step. Measure at your property, then the quiet with the source silent, so the ambient comparison is visible. The City measures on the affected property with a calibrated meter on slow response; a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement. After 10:00 p.m. the night column applies, and music takes the 5 dB(A) reduction.
rules.nextAction: While it is happening, call Alameda Police non-emergency at 510-337-8340 so an officer can hear it. The code (§4-10.8) also lets you file a written complaint about a source that exceeds the Table with the Planning Department or Public Works, stating the location, nature and extent of the noise; Code Enforcement is at 510-747-6818 during business hours. Send the dated log and PDF.

Phone estimate at your spot, not the officer's meter at the code's measurement point.

rules.title: Weekdays 7 to 7, Saturdays 8 to 5, no Sundays; outside that, the table applies
rules.summary: Alameda Municipal Code §4-10.5(b)(10) makes construction outside 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. Monday through Friday and 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. on Saturdays a prohibited act; there are no Sunday hours. The ban does not apply to work that needs no City permit, to emergency work, to a person working on their own principal residence or rental property, or where the City Manager grants an exception for significant financial hardship. Inside those hours construction noise is exempt from the exterior standards (§4-10.7(e)); outside them, and for exempt work, the receiving-property table still applies: 55 dB(A) by day and 50 dB(A) at night for more than 30 minutes an hour at a home, stepping up to a never-exceed 75/70 (§4-10.4). Loading, unloading and handling of building materials between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. that disturbs a home is its own violation, and vibration felt at the property line is another (§4-10.5(b)(7), (8)). Residential maintenance is exempt 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. weekdays and 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. weekends. Residential air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment is capped at 50 dB(A) at the receiving property (55 for older units). Each day is a separate infraction (§4-10.12).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the day, and the exact start and stop times outside the allowed hours; note the kind of work and whether a permit card is posted, since permit-free work and owner work on their own home are exempt from the hours ban. For work outside the hours or for exempt work, measure at your property and note how many minutes in the hour it ran, because the table counts minutes. The City measures on the affected property with a calibrated meter on slow response; a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement.
rules.nextAction: For work going on outside the hours, call Alameda Police non-emergency at 510-337-8340. For a project that keeps doing it, file a Code Enforcement request in Alameda's SeeClickFix and pick 'Construction Noise' from its list; include your phone and email in the description, because the form says Code Enforcement needs them to open a case. Code Enforcement is at 510-747-6818, status checks at 510-747-6845.

rules.title: Time it: ten minutes of barking inside any fifteen
rules.summary: Palo Alto Municipal Code §6.20.140 makes it unlawful to keep or permit a 'barking dog' on any premises. A barking dog is one that barks, bays, cries, howls or makes any other noise continuously and incessantly for ten minutes within a fifteen-minute period, to the disturbance of any other person. Whether to cite is up to the Animal Control Officer, and the City may also use nuisance-abatement procedures. The rule sets no dB threshold; the ten-in-fifteen clock is the test. The noise chapter adds a second angle: any animal on residential property that pushes the noise more than 6 dB above the six-minute local ambient at the property plane violates §9.10.030. Palo Alto Police Animal Control Officers serve Palo Alto, Los Altos and Los Altos Hills and handle animal-related code violations; the City's page gives dispatch at 650-329-2413 and animalcontrol@paloalto.gov.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the dog's address, the date, the exact start and stop times, and whether the barking filled ten minutes inside a fifteen-minute window with no real break; the app's level trace shows the run. If you also ran the six-minute quiet baseline, the jump over ambient supports the noise-chapter angle.

rules.title: Check 6 dB over the quiet at the property line, any hour
rules.summary: Palo Alto Municipal Code Chapter 9.10 has no fixed dB cap for homes; it works from the local ambient. No person may produce, by any machine, animal or device on residential property, a noise level more than 6 dB above the local ambient at any point outside the property plane (§9.10.030(a)). On multifamily property the same 6 dB test applies three feet from any wall, floor or ceiling inside another unit with doors and windows closed (§9.10.030(b)). Commercial and industrial property gets 8 dB over ambient; public property 15 dB at 25 feet. 'Local ambient' is the lowest level repeating itself over six minutes on a precision meter, source silent, same spot, never below 40 dBA outdoors or 30 dBA indoors (§9.10.020(d)). The rule runs all day and night; the only relief is the general daytime exception, which exempts a source that stays at or below 70 dBA at 25 feet between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Saturday, and 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on Sundays and holidays (§9.10.060(a)). Approved sound performances up to 80 dBA at 50 feet are exempt. Most violations of the chapter are misdemeanors (§9.10.080); the City Manager may issue an exception permit of up to six months.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, duration, and how it disturbed you. Measure the noise, then run the six-minute quiet baseline at the same spot with the source silent, so the difference against the 6 dB rule is visible. The City measures with a precision meter at a point outside the property plane; a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement. By day, note whether the source was still loud 25 feet away, which is where the daytime exception is judged.

rules.title: Check the 60/50 table by the minute, measured on the neighbor's property
rules.summary: South San Francisco Municipal Code Chapter 8.32 sets noise standards measured on the receiving property. In single-family and duplex zones the standard is 60 dB from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and 50 dB from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.; multifamily and downtown zones use 60 by day and 55 at night; commercial 65/60; industrial 70 any time (Table 8.32.030). A source violates the chapter if it exceeds the standard for more than 30 cumulative minutes in any hour, the standard plus 5 dB for more than 15 minutes, plus 10 dB for more than 5 minutes, plus 15 dB for more than 1 minute, or plus 20 dB for any time at all (§8.32.030(a)). A higher measured ambient replaces the standard (§8.32.030(b)). On multifamily property, noise more than 10 dB above the allowed level inside another unit, three feet from a wall with doors and windows closed, is a separate violation (§8.32.040). Independently, any wilful loud, unnecessary or unusual noise that disturbs the peace of a neighborhood is unlawful (§8.32.030(d)). Amplified sound in public needs a Police Chief permit and is limited to 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. (§§8.32.070–080). Exceeding the limits is prima facie evidence of a violation and a public nuisance (§8.32.090); each day is a misdemeanor (§8.32.110). By day, complaints go to the Engineering Division or Code Enforcement Officer; when that office is closed, to the Police (§8.32.100).

Measure at your property, then run the six-minute quiet baseline with the source silent, so the ambient comparison is visible. The City measures with a Type 1 meter five feet above ground on the receiving property, so a phone estimate is supporting evidence, not that measurement. After 10:00 p.m. the night column applies.

rules.title: Check 10 dB over the ambient base at the line; 60 by day, 45 at night is the floor
rules.summary: San Bruno Municipal Code Chapter 6.16 (rewritten by Ord. 1897, 2021) works from an 'ambient base level'. In residential zones the base is never lower than 60 decibels from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and 45 decibels from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.; where the real ambient is higher, the real ambient is the base (§6.16.030). Any noise more than 10 decibels above that base at the property plane, at a residential zone line, on another property, or inside an adjoining apartment or condo unit is prima facie evidence of a violation; between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. the base may be exceeded by up to 20 decibels for no more than 30 minutes in any 24 hours (§6.16.050). Machinery, pumps, fans and air conditioners have the same 10-dB rule (§6.16.060). Independently, any wilful loud, unnecessary or unusual noise that disturbs the peace or quiet of a neighborhood is unlawful, judged by twelve factors including level, time, duration, recurrence and closeness to bedrooms (§6.16.170). A violation that annoys people of normal sensitiveness is a public nuisance (§6.16.040). Measurements are A-weighted, slow response (§6.16.020). Amplified sound in public needs a registration with the City Manager and runs 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. (§§6.16.100–160).

rules.title: Time it for the County rule; the City adds a 50-foot test
rules.summary: Walnut Creek Municipal Code §5-1.01 adopts the Contra Costa County Animal Control Ordinance (Division 416) and hands enforcement to County Animal Services. Under the County's noisy-animal rule an animal violates when its noise disturbs a person and lasts at least 30 continuous minutes, or at least 60 intermittent minutes in a 24-hour period, at any hour; the County sets no dB threshold, sends a warning letter with a 15-day compliance period, and takes a second report as a notarized affidavit within 60 days. The City's penalty section (§5-1.02) lets Animal Services issue administrative fines of $100, $200 and $500 for a barking-dog violation on an officer's own observation or on a complaint signed under penalty of perjury. The City's own noise article adds a second angle: keeping an animal that causes frequent or continuous noise disturbing anyone nearby is a loud noise (§4-6.203(e)), and animal noise plainly audible 50 feet from the source is prima facie evidence of a violation, punishable as an infraction or misdemeanor (§4-6.207).

Step 50 feet from the source and note whether it was plainly audible there for the City's test. Keep the log through the County's 15-day compliance period, because the second report is a sworn affidavit. A phone dB estimate does not decide either rule.

rules.summary: Walnut Creek Municipal Code Chapter 4-6, Article 2 bans any loud, excessive or unreasonable noise in the City (§4-6.204). Playing a radio, instrument, phonograph or other sound device so as to disturb the peace, quiet and comfort of people on a street or in or near a home or business is a listed loud noise, and music plainly audible 50 feet from its source is prima facie evidence of a violation, at any time of day (§4-6.203(a)). Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling or singing on a public street with intent to disturb is listed too (§4-6.203(d)). Commercial loudspeakers need a Police Chief permit and are held to 50 feet and daytime hours (§4-6.203(b)). The article sets no dB limit. A violation is a misdemeanor or an infraction (§4-6.207) and a public nuisance the Police Chief or Community Development Director may abate (§4-6.208). Emergencies are exempt (§4-6.205).

The Chief of Code Enforcement (for buildings) or the City Engineer (for grading) may allow other hours when public health and safety are not impaired and someone would otherwise suffer loss, and may issue three-day emergency permits. Public utilities need no permit but must minimize noise. Separately, noise-creating landscaping and home maintenance equipment, including hammers, blowers, trimmers, mowers, chainsaws, power fans and any engine, may run only 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. on weekdays and 9:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. on weekends and holidays (§4-6.203(g)); businesses in the core area and schools may start at 7:00 a.m. on weekdays (§4-6.205). rules.summary: Cupertino Municipal Code §10.48.061 makes it unlawful and a nuisance to keep on any lot any animal, including fowl, which by any sound or cry habitually disturbs the peace and comfort of any person in the reasonable and comfortable enjoyment of life or property. The rule sets no minute or dB threshold; 'habitually' is the test. The animal title separately bars letting an animal interfere with the reasonable and comfortable use of property by barking, howling, baying or making any other noise (Title 8). The noise chapter's table also reaches animal noise: a source on residential property may not exceed 60 dBA by day or 50 dBA at night measured at the complaint site on the receiving property (§10.48.040), where daytime is 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. on weekdays and 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on weekends. Any violation of the chapter is a misdemeanor (§10.48.070), enforced by the City's Noise Control Officer, which is the Code Enforcement Division. Cupertino 311 has an Animal Concern request with a 'Barking Dog' issue type.

rules.summary: Cupertino Municipal Code §10.48.040 caps noise from a residential source at 60 dBA in the daytime and 50 dBA at night, measured at the complaint site on the receiving property; nonresidential sources get 65/55. Daytime is 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. on weekdays and 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. on weekends; everything else is nighttime (§10.48.010). Brief daytime incidents are allowed only if the minutes of excess plus the dBA over the limit add up to no more than 20 in any two-hour period, for example 5 dBA over for 15 minutes or 10 dBA over for 10 minutes (§10.48.050). Inside a multifamily building, noise may not exceed 45 dBA five feet from a wall in the next unit by day or 40 dBA from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. (§10.48.054). Independently, no person may unreasonably make or continue a 'noise disturbance', meaning sound that annoys or disturbs a reasonable person of normal sensitivities or endangers health or property (§§10.48.010, 10.48.060). The Social Host chapter (10.05) separately holds hosts responsible for loud parties. Sound level is the maximum continuous or repeated peak on an A-weighted meter. A verbal or written warning comes first unless the person is plainly not trying to comply; then citation, complaint or abatement (§10.48.011). Any violation is a misdemeanor (§10.48.070).

Other construction is banned on holidays (New Year's, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas) and at night unless it meets the night table (50 dBA at a home). A homeowner using domestic tools on their own single home may work on holidays 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. (§10.48.029). Construction helicopters are limited to 9:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m. weekdays. Landscape equipment runs 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. weekdays and 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. weekends and holidays, and only certified leaf blowers are allowed (§10.48.051). Emergencies are exempt and the Noise Control Officer may grant special exceptions after notifying neighbors (§§10.48.030–031). Any violation is a misdemeanor (§10.48.070).

rules.summary: Newark's animal title (Title 6) has no barking or noisy-animal section; it covers licensing, animals at large, bites, humane care and tethering. rules.title: Habitual barking: police warning, then two complaints or an officer's own ears
rules.summary: Napa Municipal Code §6.04.220 makes it unlawful to knowingly keep a dog that habitually barks, howls or yelps to the great discomfort of the peace and quiet of the neighborhood, or so as to materially disturb or annoy people of ordinary sensibilities; such dogs are declared a public nuisance. The section writes out the process: when someone complains to the Police Department, police notify the owner to take whatever steps are needed. If the warning does not work, either a verified complaint from at least two citizens who are not from the same family is presented to the Police Department, or an officer personally observes and confirms the barking after the department has received at least two complaints within any 30-day period; the police then inform the owner and cite. The rule sets no minute or dB threshold. Napa's noise chapter (8.08) has no animal section.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the dog's address, the date, exact start and stop times, how often it recurs, and how it disturbed you. Note the date of your first complaint to the police and of the owner's warning, because the citation path needs either a second household to sign a verified complaint or two complaints inside 30 days plus an officer's own confirmation. A neighbor from another household who hears it is worth asking now. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule.
rules.nextAction: Call Napa Police non-emergency dispatch at 707-257-9223 with the dog's exact address and your name and number; that first complaint triggers the owner's warning. If the barking continues, call again within 30 days so an officer can confirm it, or bring a second household in on a verified complaint. Napa County Animal Services handles other animal matters under a City-County contract.

rules.title: Amplified sound heard outside needs a permit; loud parties fall to state law

Commercial activity that can be heard at a residential property line between 9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. needs a permit (§8.08.020). Chapter 9.70 lets the City bill police response costs and civil penalties of $500 to $1,000 for parties where minors drink. A loud party or music that disturbs neighbors is otherwise handled by Napa Police under California Penal Code §415, which makes maliciously and willfully disturbing another person by loud and unreasonable noise an offense at any hour, with no dB cutoff.

Note whether it continued after a request to stop, because willfulness matters under Penal Code §415. A phone estimate is supporting evidence of how loud it was; no City number decides a party complaint.

rules.title: Habitual barking: an officer's visit first, then a three-household petition with two-week logs
rules.summary: Vacaville Municipal Code Chapter 6.20 declares any dog, cat or other animal whose habitual howling, yelping, barking or other noise disturbs the comfort, peace or quiet of nearby property, or would annoy a reasonable person of normal sensitivity, a public nuisance (§6.20.010). The chapter runs on a petition (§6.20.020): a writing signed by three or more persons from separate residences in the neighborhood, or by one or more residents who show the animal control officer a good-faith effort to get other signatures (or that there are fewer than three occupied homes nearby) plus adequate evidence. Vacaville contracts animal control to Humane Animal Services, which says it first sends an officer to talk to the owner as a courtesy; if the barking continues you request the Petition for Abatement of Animal as a Public Nuisance, which needs at least three signatures from different residences and a two-week noise log from each signer. The officer then issues a seven-day abatement notice, and a still-noisy animal goes to the City's hearing officer. Provoked barking does not count. The rule sets no minute or dB threshold.

Note the date of your first call and of the officer's visit to the owner. Line up two neighbors from other households now; their logs must cover the same stretch. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule.

If it continues, ask them for the Petition for Abatement, gather three households' signatures and two-week logs, and return it. rules.summary: Vacaville has no stand-alone noise chapter and no residential decibel limit. Its nuisance chapter makes excessive noise in a residential neighborhood that disturbs the peace or quiet of nearby properties, or would annoy reasonable persons of normal sensitivity, a public nuisance (§8.10.060(M)). The same paragraph says the City is not required to investigate such a complaint unless it receives a written request to abate signed by three or more persons having separate residences in the neighborhood; it may still act on a writing from fewer residents who show a good-faith effort to get the other signatures or that fewer than three homes are occupied nearby. A separate line bans commercial equipment such as parking-lot sweepers, leaf blowers and mowers within 500 feet of an occupied residence 7:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday and all day Sundays and holidays (§8.10.060(N)). Loudspeakers and amplifiers on streets, parks and other public property need a police registration and may run only 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m., never commercially on Sundays or holidays (Chapter 9.16). A loud party on private property while it is happening is a police matter under California Penal Code §415, which makes maliciously and willfully disturbing another person by loud and unreasonable noise an offense at any hour, with no dB cutoff.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, duration, what was heard, whether it was amplified, and how it disturbed you. Note whether it continued after a request to stop, because willfulness matters under Penal Code §415. Because the City wants three households' signatures before it must investigate, ask two neighbors from other homes to keep their own dates. A phone estimate shows how loud it was; no City number decides this rule.
rules.nextAction: While it is happening, call Vacaville Police non-emergency at 707-449-5200 so an officer can hear it. For a repeat address, email Code Enforcement at Code.Enforcement@cityofvacaville.gov (707-449-5693, 8:00 a.m.–5:30 p.m. weekdays, closed every other Friday) with the dates and the PDF as a written request to abate; a request signed by three households obliges the City to investigate.
rules.officialSourceLabel: Vacaville Municipal Code §8.10.060(M)–(N); Chapter 9.16; California Penal Code §415

rules.title: Within 500 feet of a home: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday, nothing on Sundays or holidays
rules.summary: Vacaville Municipal Code §8.10.060(O) declares construction, repair work or grading within 500 feet of any occupied residence between 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday a public nuisance, and allows no such work at all on Sundays or holidays. Three carve-outs: City projects; an exception granted by the Department of Public Works for emergency work, to offset weather delays, for 24-hour projects or similar; and interior work or construction, repair or grading that a homeowner does or directs at their own residence on a Sunday or holiday, which is allowed only 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. The rule sets no dB limit. Code Enforcement (part of the Fire Department) enforces the nuisance chapter and can issue a notice to abate and administrative fines (§8.10.070).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the day, whether it was a Sunday or holiday, and the exact start and stop times; note whether it was outdoor construction, repair or grading and whether the site is within 500 feet of an occupied home (it usually is if you can hear it from yours). Note any posted Public Works exception and whether the work was a homeowner's own Sunday job. A time-stamped photo or short clip is strong here because the rule turns on the clock, not on dB.
rules.nextAction: Email Code Enforcement at Code.Enforcement@cityofvacaville.gov with the site address, the dates and times and the PDF, or call 707-449-5693 (8:00 a.m.–5:30 p.m. weekdays, closed every other Friday); an inspection is scheduled as soon as possible. For work going on right now outside the hours, at night or on a Sunday, call Vacaville Police non-emergency at 707-449-5200.

hoursRule.context: Vacaville Code 8.10.060(O): construction, repair work or grading within 500 feet of an occupied residence is a nuisance between 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday, and is not allowed on Sundays or holidays, except City projects, a Public Works exception, or a homeowner's own Sunday/holiday work 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. The rule is hours-only, with no dB limit.
hoursRule.sourceQuote: Construction, repair work or grading within 500 feet from any occupied residence between the hours of seven o'clock p.m. and seven o'clock a.m. Monday through Saturday. No such construction, repair work or grading activities shall be allowed on Sundays or holidays.

rules.title: Persistent barking is banned; the fix runs through a three-household petition
rules.summary: Fairfield bans keeping any animal, crowing rooster or fowl which by any persistent sound or cry disturbs a reasonable person owning, using or occupying property in the neighborhood (City Code §25.1404, Animals and fowl), and its Table 25.1401 residential limits do not exempt barking dogs (§25.1405(A)). The abatement path is Chapter 3, Article V: an animal whose habitual howling, yelping, barking or other noise disturbs the comfort, peace or quiet of nearby property is a public nuisance (§3.60), started by a petition (§3.61(f)): a writing signed by three or more persons from separate residences in the neighborhood, or by one or more residents who show the animal control officer a good-faith effort to get other signatures (or that three or fewer homes are occupied nearby) plus adequate evidence. Fairfield contracts animal control to Humane Animal Services, which says it first sends an officer to speak with the owner; if it continues you request the Petition for Abatement, which needs at least three signatures from different residences and a two-week noise log from each signer, then a seven-day abatement notice, then the City's hearing officer. Provoked barking does not count. No minute or dB threshold decides it.
rules.captureInstruction: Log every episode with the animal's address, the date, exact start and stop times, and how it disturbed you; keep it going for at least two straight weeks, because each petition signer must hand in a two-week log. Note the date of your first call and of the officer's visit to the owner. Line up two neighbors from other households now; their logs must cover the same stretch. A phone dB estimate does not decide this no-threshold rule.
rules.nextAction: Call Humane Animal Services at 707-449-1700 (8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., seven days) with the animal's exact address, when it barks and your name and number; an officer will speak with the owner. If it continues, ask them for the Petition for Abatement, gather three households' signatures and two-week logs, and return it. After hours, Fairfield Police non-emergency 707-428-7300 can dispatch them.

rules.title: At the property line: 50 dB by day, 45 dB at night, and 5 dB lower for music
rules.summary: Fairfield City Code §25.1403 makes it unlawful to create noise anywhere in the City that exposes other properties to more than Table 25.1401. For a residential receiver, measured at the property line of the receiving property, the exterior limits are 50 dB Leq by day (7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.) and 45 dB Leq at night (10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.), with maximum levels (Lmax) of 70 dB by day and 65 dB at night; each limit drops 5 dB for simple tones, noise consisting primarily of speech or music, or recurring impulsive noise, so a party's music is held to 45 Leq by day and 40 Leq at night. Leq is defined as the energy average over a sample period, typically one hour. Where the existing ambient already exceeds the table, a new source must be mitigated down to the ambient. Separately, §25.1404 bans using any musical instrument, amplifier or sound device so that a reasonable person owning, using or occupying property in the neighborhood is disturbed, with no number at all, and §12.8 bans unnecessary noises annoying to persons of ordinary sensitiveness. Chapter 12, Article VII lets police bill a responsible person for repeat responses to a loud party. Enforcement is by administrative citation (§25.1413). Property-maintenance tools are exempt 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m., and permitted special events are exempt in the same hours.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the source address, exact times, duration, what was heard, whether it was music or speech (that triggers the 5 dB lower limit), and how it disturbed you. Measure from your own property line facing the source if you can, and note where you stood; the City's limit is read at the receiving property line with a sound level meter. If the source falls quiet, capture the quiet level at the same spot, because the ambient sets the floor. Note whether it continued after a request to stop.
rules.nextAction: While it is happening, call Fairfield Police non-emergency at 707-428-7300 and press option 8 for a dispatcher; the City's own MyFairfieldCA portal says noise complaints go to that line. For a repeat address, email Code Enforcement at fpdcodeenforcement@fairfield.ca.gov (707-428-7587) with the dates, times and the PDF.

meterLimit.comparisonContext: Fairfield Code Table 25.1401: a residential property line may receive 50 dB Leq by day (7 a.m.–10 p.m.) and 45 dB Leq at night, each lowered by 5 dB for noise that is mostly speech or music, so music is held to 45 by day and 40 at night; Lmax limits are 70 by day and 65 at night, also 5 dB lower for music. Leq is an energy average over a sample period, typically one hour, read at the receiving property line. Phone estimate at your spot, not the officer's meter at the code's measurement point.

ambientRecipe.note: Fairfield reads its limits as an hour-long energy average and says a new source only has to come down to the existing ambient where the ambient is already above the table. Capture the quiet level at your property line with the source silent so the PDF shows the floor the City would use.
ambientRecipe.sourceQuote: In situations where the existing ambient noise level exceeds the noise levels indicated in the above table, any new noise source must include mitigation that reduces the noise level to the existing ambient level.

rules.title: Construction tools are silent 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. every day, unless Public Works says otherwise in writing
rules.summary: Fairfield City Code §25.1404 (Construction activities) bans operating, or permitting the operation of, any tools or equipment used in construction, grading or demolition between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., except by written permission of the Director of Public Works. The ban runs every day of the week; the code sets no separate weekend or holiday hours. Inside 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. construction still has to meet the residential property-line limits of Table 25.1401 (50 dB Leq and 70 dB Lmax by day, 5 dB lower for impulsive noise), and large-truck deliveries and loading next to homes 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. may not exceed the Lmax limits. Property-maintenance tools such as mowers, blowers and power tools are exempt 7:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. (§25.1405(B)). Enforcement is by administrative citation under Chapter 1, Article II (§25.1413).
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the day, and the exact start and stop times; the clock decides this rule, so any work before 7:00 a.m. or after 10:00 p.m. is the fact that matters. Note whether it was construction, grading or demolition tools rather than yard tools, and whether a Public Works permission is posted. A time-stamped photo or short clip is strong here. For daytime work that is very loud, a reading at your property line matters against the 70 dB Lmax and 50 dB Leq lines.
rules.nextAction: For work going on right now between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., call Fairfield Police non-emergency at 707-428-7300, option 8. For a project that keeps doing it, email Code Enforcement at fpdcodeenforcement@fairfield.ca.gov (707-428-7587) with the site address, the dated log and the PDF; ask whether the project holds written permission from Public Works.

meterLimit.comparisonContext: Fairfield Code Table 25.1401: a residential property line may receive 50 dB Leq by day (7 a.m.–10 p.m.) and 45 dB Leq at night, with Lmax limits of 70 by day and 65 at night, read at the receiving property line; night construction is banned outright by 25.1404 regardless of level. Phone estimate at your spot, not the officer's meter at the code's measurement point.

rules.title: Ten minutes of noise in any hour is the line; two households or an officer's ears prove it
rules.summary: Petaluma Municipal Code §9.08.180 bans keeping any animal on premises in the city that continuously and incessantly produces noise at any time of day or night to the disturbance of any other person. Continuous and incessant means noise for an aggregate period of ten minutes or more in any one-hour period that disturbs the peace of another person, including barking, howling, crying, baying or squealing, provided nobody was trespassing or threatening to trespass on the owner's property and the animal was not being teased or provoked. An animal control officer investigates every reported incident, writes a report signed under penalty of perjury, appends the signed statements of witnesses, victims and the owner, and requires each of them to keep a bark/noise log listing times and durations, also signed under penalty of perjury. A rebuttable presumption of a public nuisance exists when at least two individuals from separate residences sign a declaration under penalty of perjury to facts showing a violation, or a law enforcement or animal control officer personally witnesses one. Each day the noise continues is a separate offense. The City contracts its animal services to Marin Humane, which took over on April 1. The rule sets no dB level.
rules.captureInstruction: For each incident record the animal's address, the date, the exact start and stop times, and how many minutes of noise fell inside each clock hour; ten aggregate minutes in one hour is the City's line, so an hour with 6 minutes, then 3, then 2 counts. Note whether anyone was near the owner's fence or provoking the animal, because that defeats the rule. Keep the log going after your first call, since the officer will ask you to sign it under penalty of perjury; a neighbor from a second household who hears it and will sign a declaration makes the case presumptive. A phone dB estimate does not decide this minutes-based rule.
rules.nextAction: Call Marin Humane at 415-883-4621 with the animal's exact address, the dates and times, and your name and number; the City's own answer page sends barking complaints there. An animal control officer will open a report and ask you and any witnesses to keep a signed bark/noise log; hand over the PDF log with it.

rules.title: A quiet city by law: 70 dB by day, 65 at night, read on your own property over 15 minutes
rules.summary: Petaluma's Implementing Zoning Ordinance §21.040(A) declares Petaluma a quiet city and sets Table 21.1, Maximum Exterior Noise Exposure in Leq dBA, measured on the property where the noise disturbance is being experienced, in its outdoor spaces (§21.040(A)(4)(c)). Night runs 10:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m. Monday through Friday and 10:00 p.m.–8:00 a.m. on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. Noise lasting a cumulative 15 minutes or more in an hour may not exceed 65 dBA at night or 70 by day; 5 minutes or more, 70 at night or 75 by day; 1 minute or more, 75 at night or 80 by day; the General Plan ambient line is 60. If the measured ambient is above 60 dB the standard is raised in 5 dB steps to cover it, never above 75; at an ambient of 70 or more the ambient itself becomes the limit. Separately, using any loudspeaker or similar device so as to create a noise disturbance is a public nuisance at any hour (§21.040(A)(3)(a)(9)), and a public address system may run only 10:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. and no more than 5 dBA above ambient (§21.040(A)(3)(d)). The Noise Control Officer is the Community Development Director together with the Police Chief.
rules.captureInstruction: Measure from your own property, outdoors, with the phone about four to five feet off the ground and at least ten feet from walls or fences; that is where the City's meter would sit. Let the meter run at least 15 minutes when you can, because the strictest line is the 15-minute cumulative average. Record the source address, exact times, whether it was a weekday or a weekend/holiday, whether it was amplified, and how it disturbed you. If the source pauses, capture the quiet level at the same spot, because the ambient can raise the limit.
rules.nextAction: While it is happening, call Petaluma Police non-emergency at 707-778-4372 so an officer can hear it. For a repeat address, file the Code Enforcement complaint form on the City site (Neighborhood Preservation, 707-778-4469, codeenforcement@cityofpetaluma.org, Monday–Thursday) with the dates, times and the PDF.

meterLimit.comparisonContext: Petaluma IZO Table 21.1: on the receiving property's outdoor space, noise lasting 15 or more cumulative minutes in an hour may not exceed 70 dBA Leq by day (7 a.m.–10 p.m. weekdays; 8 a.m.–10 p.m. weekends and holidays) or 65 at night; shorter bursts get 5 dB more per step (5 minutes: 75/70, 1 minute: 80/75); an ambient above 60 raises the line in 5 dB steps, never past 75. Phone estimate at your spot, not the officer's meter at the code's measurement point.

ambientRecipe.note: Petaluma's measurement rule reads the ambient first, on the receiver's property, A-weighted, slow response, microphone four to five feet up and ten feet or more from any reflective surface, with the offending source shut off if possible. An ambient above 60 dB raises Table 21.1 in 5 dB steps, never above 75. Capture the quiet level at the same spot with the source silent so the PDF shows the floor the City would use.
ambientRecipe.sourceQuote: Utilizing the “A” weighting scale of a sound level meter and the “slow” meter response (use “fast” response for impulsive type sounds), the ambient noise level shall first be measured at a position or positions at any point on the receiver’s property which can include private and public property. In general, the microphone shall be located four to five feet above the ground; ten feet or more from the nearest reflective surface where possible. If possible, the ambient noise shall be measured with the alleged offending noise source inoperative.

rules.title: Tools and construction: 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. weekdays, 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. weekends and holidays
rules.summary: Petaluma's Implementing Zoning Ordinance §21.040(A)(3)(a) declares it a public nuisance to operate, before 7:00 a.m. or after 10:00 p.m. daily, and before 9:00 a.m. or after 10:00 p.m. on Saturdays, Sundays and state, federal or local holidays, any of a listed set of sources: a hammer or anything used to repeatedly pound or strike; impact wrenches and compressed-air tools; any internal-combustion tool such as a chain saw, backpack blower or lawn mower; any electric or battery tool for cutting, drilling or shaping such as a saw, drill, lathe or router; heavy equipment, drilling and boring rigs, cranes, generators and pumps, pavement breakers, pile drivers, rollers, sand blasters, trenchers and concrete trucks, including loading and unloading them; and construction, demolition, excavation, erection, alteration or repair activity itself. The Noise Control Officer may issue an urgent-necessity exemption permit for up to ten working days, renewable to 90 days. Inside the allowed hours, Table 21.1 still caps the noise on the receiving property at 70 dBA Leq by day for 15 cumulative minutes an hour (75 for 5 minutes, 80 for 1 minute), 5 dB lower at night. Emergency responses, airport, river and railroad operations, garbage and utility vehicles, and uses with their own conditions of approval are exempt.
rules.captureInstruction: Record the site address, the day, whether it was a weekend or holiday, and the exact start and stop times; the clock decides this rule, so any tool before 7:00 a.m. (9:00 a.m. on weekends and holidays) or after 10:00 p.m. is the fact that matters. Name the tool or machine you heard, since the ordinance lists them. Note whether an exemption permit is posted. A time-stamped photo or short clip is strong here. For loud daytime work, a 15-minute reading from your own property matters against the 70 dBA line.
rules.nextAction: File the Code Enforcement complaint form on the City site with the site address, the dates and times and the PDF; Neighborhood Preservation staff answer 707-778-4469 and codeenforcement@cityofpetaluma.org Monday through Thursday. For work going on right now outside the hours, call Petaluma Police non-emergency at 707-778-4372.
